payload:
- A cell's background processes do not outlive its entry on Windows (1-2.2). Consequences: a harness timeout on the entry ends the cell (the Claude Code
  shell tools stop a foreground command at 2 minutes by default and 10 at most), so **long cells are launched as background tasks**; a cell child that
  asks for `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` now fails; a cell ended mid-write can leave `.git/index.lock` behind, which the witness tree does not show.
- **`ABNORMAL_END` means "no process in the run's job remains", not "nothing of the run is running".** Work a cell hands to a broker outside its job —
  a COM/DCOM out-of-process server, WMI `Win32_Process.Create`, Task Scheduler, `wsl.exe` (Linux processes in the WSL VM), `docker run`, ShellExecute
  to an already-running application — is not in the job and survives it; release is a human act for this reason.
- A persistent `CELL_ALIVE` (another process keeps a handle to the job) has no in-tool way out: the holder is found and closed outside the tool, outside
  the trust boundary.
- If the entry is in a job whose limits forbid nested assignment of its child, launching fails closed (`JOB_UNAVAILABLE`); the probes ran nested and passed.

## 1. Change request — the rule register

**Each rule below is the canonical text of that rule; every other section of this order refers to it by its ID and does not restate it**
(user ruling "1:A", 2026-10-18: the common cause of the loop-4 findings was one rule written in several places). Groups: **G** gates read by the
promotion decision (user condition ①), **B** the brief (user condition ②), **O** output, **T** selftests, **M** manufacture.

### G — check results read by the promotion decision (G1 in §0)

- **G1 — the declared set.** A register entry may carry `required_gates: [ID, ...]`: the check IDs whose results the promotion decision must read
  (control-plan row IDs `CP-*` in a product; the order's acceptance IDs `V*` and `inspection` in this repository). The order carries the same list on
  exactly one line that starts with `required_gates:` at column 0, outside fenced blocks and HTML comments (the fence and comment handling bomdd-job
  already uses for the equipment lines, `bomdd-job.py:73-79`). The order is the ruling record and the register field is its machine copy. Changing the
  set after filing means changing the order's line, with the ruling that changes the acceptance written next to it, and the register field together.
  The register template (`method/templates/60-change-register.yaml`) documents the field.
- **G2 — bomdd-job's projection.** bomdd-job projects `required_gates` with its source coordinate; absent in both → `null`, source `none`. Any of these
  → `LEDGER_INCONSISTENT` (ledger-derivable): not a list of non-empty strings; a duplicate ID; more than one G1 line in the order; the order's line
  absent or unparsable while the field is present, or the reverse; the two lists not equal as sets.
- **G3 — the promotion check.** Only when the job's state is verified (the promotion decision; R11's anchor), after the witness verifies ADVANCE, `decide()`
  applies, in this order: (1) R11 unchanged — an inspector declared and no `inspection` gate → `STOP INSPECTION_MISSING`; (2) the field absent or empty
  → `UNMEASURABLE`, code `GATES_UNDECLARED`; (3) every ID of the set (`inspection` included) must equal, as an exact string, the name of a gate in the
  witness, else `UNMEASURABLE`, code `REQUIRED_GATE_MISSING`, naming the IDs. Codes (2) and (3): stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, delivery operator.
  A red gate is refused by the witness as today (every gate must exit 0); gates beyond the set are allowed. The decision record carries
  `required_gates` and the matched gate names. In other states the set is not checked, so factory and inspection cells launch before their gates exist.
- **G4 — what "read" means.** The decision reads each required gate's **declared** exit in the witness and does not re-run the check (witness W2, limit
  (2)); re-measurement stays the acceptance side's duty. A control-plan row keeps `fixture` and `oracle` as its mapping to the checker; the only new
  convention is that the row's witness gate is named by the row's `id`.
- **G5 — operator-layer.md.** The core gets the description convention only (a gate is named by its check row ID; the register's `required_gates`, equal
  to the order's line, lists them; an absent field is not a pass). The sentence that a mechanism reads them goes to the adapter A1 (the core claims no
  mechanism, §7).

### B — the brief kept and re-fetchable (G2 in §0)

- **B1 — the option.** `--brief PATH|none` is required with `--cell` and refused without it (`ARG_ERROR` either way); `none` with `--report` →
  `ARG_ERROR` (a reporting cell is an inspection or factory cell and has a brief); `none` alone declares a cell with no brief and is recorded.
  These checks run **after every existing argument check**, so a missing or misplaced `--brief` never hides another argument error.
- **B2 — the store.** `<git-common-dir>/bomdd-run/briefs/<ECO>/<sha256>`: one directory per ECO, one file per distinct brief named by its sha256
  (64 lowercase hex); one store per clone whatever `--ledger` says and whichever worktree runs; outside every worktree. It is written only after
  `decide()` returns ADVANCE for a launching invocation, before the decision record and before the cell starts; a refused invocation stores nothing.
  Steps: read the bytes; a brief containing `\r` → `BRIEF_NOT_LF` (the repository declares `* text=auto eol=lf`, so a CRLF brief would be committed
  as other bytes); compute sha256; an existing store file is re-hashed and must match; otherwise write a `.tmp-<random>` file in the same directory and
  `os.replace` it to the final name; a failed replace is accepted if the final name now exists and re-hashes to its name; re-read the stored file and
  compare. Any failure → the decision becomes `UNMEASURABLE` before the decision record is written (code `BRIEF_UNREADABLE`, `BRIEF_NOT_LF` or
  `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`, stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, delivery operator), and nothing launches.
- **B3 — the record.** The decision record carries `brief: {path, sha256, size, store_ref}`; `store_ref` is the stored file's path, the reference from
  which the original bytes are re-fetched on this clone. The cell receives `BOMDD_BRIEF` = that path. The store directory's 64-hex files are the set of
  briefs launched for the ECO on this clone (no index file).
- **B4 — the committed copy, checked at promotion.** When the job's state is verified, after G3, `decide()` lists the ECO's store directory, takes only
  64-hex names and re-hashes each (bytes not matching the name → `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`); other entries (left-over `.tmp-*`) are ignored and listed in the
  decision record. Every stored brief must exist in the tree the decision binds (the witness-verified worktree tree, `rec.tree`) under `bomdd/reports/`
  with the same sha256 — found with `git ls-tree -r <tree> -- bomdd/reports/`, read with `git cat-file blob`. Otherwise `UNMEASURABLE`, code
  `BRIEF_NOT_COMMITTED` (naming the sha256 prefixes); a store directory that cannot be listed → `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`; stop type `MISSING_INPUT`,
  delivery operator. The decision record gets `brief_copies: [{sha256, path, tree}]`. **The lasting reference is `{sha256, path}`**; `tree` only binds
  the pair to this decision (an unreferenced tree object can be pruned).
- **B5 — the command.** The command string is not altered (R5).

### O — output

- **O1 — codes and the first line.** The codes from G3 and B (`GATES_UNDECLARED`, `REQUIRED_GATE_MISSING`, `BRIEF_*`) go in a field of their own,
  `entry_code`; the existing `code` keeps the witness code. The first output line (R7) gets a tag per new code (as `INSPECTION_MISSING` has,
  `bomdd-run.py:345-363`), so it never reads as the witness's `OK`.

### T — selftests (derived from the recorded inventory, not from memory)

**Evidence:** [`bomdd/reports/eco-112-arm-inventory/`](reports/eco-112-arm-inventory/README.md) — an `ast` extraction of every selftest call that can
carry `--cell`, the dynamic log of one selftest run, their cross-check, and a one-call-at-a-time mutation, measured on `bomdd-run.py` at `3a9de06`
(sha256 `b028bc53…`): **12 call sites, 56 calls with `--cell`, no gap; 29 calls noticed by their own check, 26 MASKED, 1 CRASH**; two existing
arms (`kb-ledger-unwritable`, `kb-ledger-inside`) pass today for another reason (their calls lack `--executor`, so the ECO-072 executor check refuses them first).

- **T1 — the 56 calls.** Each of the 56 calls, by site (the evidence lists them), gains a valid `--brief`: a fixture brief where `--report` is set (the R10
  report arms, `stale`, `dirtarget`, the cell-exit arm, the `rep-arg` loop), `none` elsewhere. Dry invocations get no `--brief`.
- **T2 — own reasons.** Every arm that expects a refusal asserts its own reason in the first line (and, where it reads the ledger, that a record for this
  call exists), not only the verdict prefix. Where a code is shared by several reasons (`ARG_ERROR`), the arm checks a message fragment unique to its own
  reason; a code alone suffices only where it names the reason (`BRIEF_NOT_LF`, `REQUIRED_GATE_MISSING`, …).
- **T3 — existing defects repaired.** The two arms that pass for another reason today get `--executor`, so their own reasons fire; the cell-exit-7 arm's
  `unlink` of its report is guarded (`missing_ok=True`, `bomdd-run.py:693`), so a refused call is reported by that arm's own check, not by a crash.
- **T4 — new arms.** Each of G1-G3, B1-B4 and O1 gets a known-bad arm that goes red for that rule's own reason (the observations are listed in §3 V1 and
  V2). The selftest fixtures (ECO-900 to ECO-905) are given `required_gates` (register and order line) where their state is verified.
- **T5 — the shape the V3 instrument reads** is a constraint on the manufactured selftest: (a) the body stays in a function named `_selftest_body`;
  (b) every invocation goes through its local helper `call`, each argv written as a list literal (or a loop over a tuple of list literals, or the `arm()`
  builder) containing `"--cell"` literally where it launches — no argv held in, or concatenated from, another variable; (c) new arms are added inside
  `_selftest_body` (directly or through `arm()`/`rep_arm()`); (d) failures are appended to its local list `fails`; (e) no real message contains
  `INSTRUMENT_MUTATION`. An instrument crash or a static/dynamic gap caused by a change of shape is **cannot measure**, not a pass, and is resolved by
  restoring the shape, not by editing the instrument.
- **T6 — the V3 instrument's scope.** It sees in-process `call(...)` invocations inside `_selftest_body`; a launch from a thread or a child process is
  outside it.

### M — manufacture

- **M1 — order.** ECO-112 is manufactured first, then ECO-113 (ECO-113's order refers to this rule); ECO-113 rebases its manufacture on ECO-112's
  verified head. So V3 is measured on a selftest that ECO-113's arms have not yet changed; ECO-113's acceptance covers its own arms. Both change
  `bomdd-run.py`, `bomdd-job.py` and `operator-layer.md`.

### Declared limits (each refers to the rule it limits)

- **L1 (G4):** declared exits, not re-measured ones. Whether a `required_gates` set is the right set is the filer's and the inspector's judgement.
- **L2 (G1, G2):** a change of the set after filing is not detected mechanically — bomdd-job checks that the order and the register agree, not that they
  still say what they said at filing; a change to both without a ruling is caught only by reading the order's history (inspection, diff audit).
- **L3 (G3):** ECO-079 (open, no field) stops with `GATES_UNDECLARED` at its promotion until its owner writes the field and the order's line.
- **L4 (B2, B4):** the store is clone-local; on another clone B4 sees an empty store and checks nothing. A brief deleted from the store by hand is outside
  the trust boundary (like deleting the witness, ECO-046).
- **L5 (B2):** on Windows, `os.replace` onto a store file another invocation holds open can fail; B2's accept-if-it-now-matches covers the same-bytes
  case, and anything else fails closed. This is the one place where ①② meet concurrency, which is ECO-113's.
- **L6 (B5):** whether the cell actually read the declared brief is not proven by the record.
- **L7 (T1-T5):** the bomdd-run and bomdd-job selftests are not run in CI (CI runs the witness selftest); they are run locally and recorded (V3).
- **L8:** in-flight runs and duplicate launches are ECO-113's.

### Not changed

- `bomdd-witness.py`, `self-conformance.py`, hooks, `.github`, the playbook, skills, `.claude/skills`, the control-plan template.
- Machine distribution to product repositories (EXP-20260914-01 stays suspended). Products get the register-template comment (G1) and the
  operator-layer text (G5) through the kit as usual.
- No scheduler, workflow engine, LLM wiki or context access control (user condition).

## 2. No-impact prediction (before manufacture; frozen at filing)

- **The diff:** `method/tools/bomdd-run.py`, `method/tools/bomdd-job.py`, `method/templates/60-change-register.yaml`,
  `method/templates/product-profile/operator-layer.md`, `method/improvements.md`, this order, the register, and `bomdd/reports/eco-112-*/`
  (briefs and reports).
- **Not touched:** `method/tools/bomdd-witness.py`, `method/tools/self-conformance.py`, hooks, `.github`, the playbook, skills, `.claude/skills`,
  `method/templates/33-control-plan.yaml`.

## 1. Change request — the rule register

**Each rule below is the canonical text of that rule; every other section of this order refers to it by its ID and does not restate it**
(user ruling "2:A", 2026-10-18). The five responsibilities stay apart and meet only in the launch sequence S1: **X** exclusion (may this entry act now),
**W** ownership (the cell lives no longer than its entry), **J** judgement (is an earlier run open, and in what state), **R** recovery (close an open
run), **A** records (commit and read lines). **S** is the launch sequence, **O** output, **T** selftests. Judgement never follows processes.

### X — exclusion

- **X1 — the lock file.** `<git-common-dir>/bomdd-run/<ECO>.lock`, one per clone whatever `--ledger` says and whichever worktree runs. It holds no
  state; bomdd-run never deletes it (deleting a held lock file on POSIX lets a second process lock a new file of the same name).
- **X2 — acquiring it.** `os.open(O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_BINARY | O_NOINHERIT)` (POSIX: `O_CLOEXEC`), then a non-blocking exclusive lock: Windows
  `msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1)` at offset 0; POSIX `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`. **Only the locking call's conflict** (Windows `EACCES`
  from `LK_NBLCK`; POSIX `EWOULDBLOCK`/`EAGAIN`) means another entry is alive → cause `ENTRY_ALIVE` (the "running" state). Any error from `os.open`,
  the directory, or any other error from the locking call → cause `LOCK_UNAVAILABLE`; its way out is fixing the environment, not recovery.
- **X3 — who holds it.** A launching invocation (`--cell`) from before classification until it returns; a release or quarantine for its whole run; a dry
  invocation only for its classification. The OS releases it when the holder's handle closes or the holder dies.

### W — ownership (Windows)

- **W1 — the job.** The launching entry creates a Job Object named `Local\BomDD-run-<ECO>-<run_id>` with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` and
  no breakaway flag. **The entry is never in the job**, so in-process callers (the selftest) are unaffected.
- **W2 — placing the cell.** The cell is started with `Popen(..., shell=True, creationflags=CREATE_SUSPENDED)` and assigned to the job through `Popen`'s
  process handle **immediately**, with nothing in between; it is resumed later, at S1's resume step. The resume finds the cell's threads by a thread
  snapshot filtered by the cell's pid, which is safe from pid reuse because the entry holds the process handle throughout. Everything the cell starts is
  in the job from creation. **No pid is used for judgement or for stopping.**
- **W3 — the handle.** The entry holds the job's only handle and closes it when the cell has ended or the wait was interrupted (in-process callers before
  `run()` returns); if the entry dies, the OS closes it. Closing it ends every process still in the job, and the job ceases to exist.
- **W4 — failing to set up.** Creating or configuring the job, or assigning the cell, fails → the suspended cell is terminated through its handle (it has
  run nothing); code `JOB_UNAVAILABLE`. What is recorded and printed is S1's. (A failed resume is S2's, not this rule's.)
- **W5 — the namespace key.** `Local\` resolves per Windows session and per AppContainer; the `start` record carries `session` (the entry's Windows
  session id) and `appcontainer` (its token's AppContainer SID, or `none`).
- **W6 — POSIX.** No job is created; nothing ties the cell to the entry.

### J — judgement

- **J1 — the source.** The run journal `<git-common-dir>/bomdd-run/<ECO>.runs.jsonl`, read only through A2. An open run is a `start` record with no
  `end`, `abort` or `release` for its `run_id`. The ledger (`--ledger`) is not read for this.
- **J2 — the classes.** Only while holding the lock (X3). No open run → proceed. An open run means its entry is gone (else X2 would have refused); it is
  classified by its job, named in its `start` record:
  - `ABNORMAL_END` — Windows; host, `session` and `appcontainer` equal to the classifier's; and opening the job by name fails with
    `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, or the job exists with 0 active processes: **no process in the run's job remains**;
  - `CELL_ALIVE` — the job exists with active processes (while the OS is still ending them, or because another process holds a handle to it, which keeps
    kill-on-close from firing);
  - `UNKNOWN` — POSIX; a host, `session` or `appcontainer` that differs or cannot be read; any other error from opening or querying the job;
  - `JOURNAL_CORRUPT` — a complete line that does not parse (A4).
  A start without an end is never read as an abnormal end by itself. Verdicts and exits: O1.

### R — recovery

- **R1 — the commands.** `bomdd-run.py ECO --release RUN_ID --by EQ-NNN` and `bomdd-run.py ECO --quarantine-journal --by EQ-NNN` take no other
  option (`--cell`, `--executor`, `--report`, `--range`, `--ledger`, `--brief` → `ARG_ERROR`). Neither runs `decide()`, launches, or stops a process.
- **R2 — release.** Takes the lock (X2), re-classifies the open run named by RUN_ID (J2): `CELL_ALIVE` refused; `ABNORMAL_END` and `UNKNOWN` closed by a
  `release` record `{run_id, classified, cause, by}`, with `cell: unverified` for `UNKNOWN` (the person releasing asserts that no process of the run is
  running). A RUN_ID that is not an open run → `ARG_ERROR`.
- **R3 — quarantine** (the way out of `JOURNAL_CORRUPT`). Takes the lock and commits into the same journal a `quarantine` record
  `{offset, excluded_sha256, by}`; complete lines before `offset` that do not parse are excluded from parsing from then on. Nothing is moved or deleted;
  every parsed open run stays open and needs its own release. Refused while any parsed open run is `CELL_ALIVE`.
- **R4 — `--by`.** Must name equipment with `kind: human`, `status: active` in `bomdd/70-equipment.yaml`; it is self-reported.
- **R5 — what recovery is not.** It does not resume or stop anything. Restarting is a new launch after the release, decided afresh on the current tree
  through the witness (R3 of the tool's spec). Resumption inside a cell is the cell's own contract.

### A — records

- **A1 — journal write.** One record = one JSON line (`ensure_ascii=True`) ending in `\n`, written by a single `os.write` on a descriptor opened with
  `O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_BINARY | O_NOINHERIT` (POSIX: `O_CLOEXEC`), then `os.fsync`. A short write or an error is a failure. Journal
  writes happen only while holding the lock (X3).
- **A2 — journal read.** Bytes split on `b"\n"` only. A final segment without `\n` is a torn record, treated as absent; the next writer, holding the lock,
  truncates the file to the last `\n` and commits a `repair` record `{truncated_bytes, sha256}`. A torn `start` precedes no started cell (S1 resumes or
  starts the cell only after `start` is committed).
- **A3 — the interface.** commit(record) → ok / failed; read() → records, torn tail, corrupt lines. Nothing else touches the journal.
- **A4 — a complete unparsable line** cannot come from bomdd-run (single writer, single write, under the lock, binary mode); it makes J2's
  `JOURNAL_CORRUPT`, and the way out is R3.
- **A5 — ledger appends.** Every ledger append (existing ones included) holds a short blocking OS lock on `<ledger path>.lock` (outside the worktree,
  like the ledger — R4 of the tool's spec); not obtained within 10 s → a ledger write failure (the existing handling).

### S — the launch sequence (where X, W, J, A meet)

- **S1 — order.** lock (X2) → classify (J2; a refusal or an open run → S4) → re-check `--report` (R10, now under the lock) → `decide()` → if ADVANCE:
  1. **Windows:** create the job (W1), start the cell suspended and assign it (W2). On W4 failure: the decision becomes `UNMEASURABLE`, code
     `JOB_UNAVAILABLE`; the ledger decision record and the first line are written with it; no `start`; return per O1.
  2. commit `start` `{run_id, job_name, entry_pid, host, session, appcontainer, started_at}` (A1). On failure: close the job handle (W3); the decision
     becomes `UNMEASURABLE`, code `JOURNAL_WRITE_FAILED`; the ledger decision record and the first line are written with it.
  3. write the ledger decision record (R4 of the tool's spec). On failure: close the job handle, commit `abort` `{run_id, reason}`, return per O1.
  4. print the first line (R7).
  5. **launch:** Windows — resume the cell (W2); POSIX — `Popen` the cell here (no job, no suspension; W6). Same terminal session, so the cell's
     prompts pass through (R5 of the tool's spec). Before this step no process of the cell has run.
  6. wait → commit `end` `{run_id, cell_exit}` (retried 3 times) → write the ledger cell record with `journal_end: committed|failed` (one added field;
     the tool's two-record shape and its readers are unchanged) → close the job handle (W3) → return.
  Codes in steps 1-2: stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, delivery operator.
- **S2 — a failed resume** (after the first line): close the job handle (the OS ends the suspended cell), commit `end` with `cell_exit: "RESUME_FAILED"`,
  write the ledger cell record with the same `cell_exit`, print the second line `cell not started (RESUME_FAILED)` (where `cell exit N` goes), return
  per O1.
- **S3 — an interrupted wait** (`KeyboardInterrupt` or an exception): commit a non-closing `interrupted` note; write the ledger cell record with
  `cell_exit: "interrupted"`, `journal_end: none`; print `cell interrupted`; close the job handle (the OS ends the cell's tree); return per O1. The run
  then reads `ABNORMAL_END` (J2) and is released (R2).
- **S4 — refusals before `decide()`** (`ENTRY_ALIVE`, `LOCK_UNAVAILABLE`, an open run): a ledger decision record (`decision`, `stop_type`
  `RUN_IN_FLIGHT`, `cause`, and the open run's `run_id` where there is one) and the line `<VERDICT> <ECO> RUN_IN_FLIGHT(<cause>) <run_id prefix>
  → operator` (within 80 columns, R7).

### O — output and vocabulary

- **O1 — verdicts and exit codes (the tool's R8, amended).** `ENTRY_ALIVE`, `ABNORMAL_END`, `CELL_ALIVE`: `STOP`, stop type `RUN_IN_FLIGHT`, exit 1.
  `LOCK_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNKNOWN`, `JOURNAL_CORRUPT`: `UNMEASURABLE`, stop type `RUN_IN_FLIGHT`, exit 2. `JOB_UNAVAILABLE`, `JOURNAL_WRITE_FAILED`:
  `UNMEASURABLE`, stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, exit 2. A launching run otherwise exits as today (0 when launched), **except S2 (`RESUME_FAILED`) and
  S3 (interrupted), which exit 2**, and S1.3's failure, which exits 2. Release and quarantine: 0 = closed, 1 = refused (`ENTRY_ALIVE`, `CELL_ALIVE`),
  2 = cannot measure or bad arguments; their first line is `RELEASED|QUARANTINED <ECO> <run_id or offset> (<classified>) by <EQ>` or S4's line.
  Delivery for every `RUN_IN_FLIGHT` cause: operator.
- **O2 — vocabulary and documents.** `RUN_IN_FLIGHT` is added to bomdd-job's stop vocabulary (not ledger-derivable; derived by the entry, like
  `INDEPENDENCE_FAIL`), to bomdd-run's delivery table (operator), and to operator-layer.md §2 (11 words). The core gets the word, its delivery, and the
  hand procedure (§7): before launching a cell by hand, confirm that no other launch of the same change is running, and write the launch and its end in
  the change order. The mechanism sentence goes to the adapter A1.

### T — selftests

- **T1 — arms.** Each rule above gets a known-bad arm that goes red for its own reason (the observations are listed in §3); a refusal arm checks a
  message fragment or code unique to its own reason, not only the verdict prefix. Existing arms keep their verdicts and their reasons.
- **T2 — shape.** New in-process calls follow ECO-112's T5 (in `_selftest_body`, through `call`); the arms that need separate processes (concurrency,
  the killed entry) run bomdd-run as a child process and are outside ECO-112's V3 instrument (ECO-112 T6).

### Manufacture

- ECO-112's **M1** governs the order: ECO-112 first, then this ECO, rebased on ECO-112's verified head.

### Declared limits (each refers to the rule it limits)

- **L1 (X2, W6, J2):** POSIX — no Job Object and no substitute; an open run whose entry is gone reads `UNKNOWN` and is released on a human assertion
  (R2's `cell: unverified`); a wrong assertion allows a duplicate launch. `flock` is not measured here (V1(g) records the branch exercised).
- **L2 (X2, W3):** a just-killed holder may read `ENTRY_ALIVE` briefly, and `CELL_ALIVE` is usually transient (OS unlock and job teardown times are not bounded).
- **L3 (J2, R2):** a persistent `CELL_ALIVE` (another process keeps a handle to the job) has no in-tool way out; the holder is found and closed outside the
  tool, outside the trust boundary.
- **L4 (J2):** `ABNORMAL_END` means "no process in the run's job remains", not "nothing of the run is running": work a cell hands to a broker outside its
  job — a COM/DCOM out-of-process server, WMI `Win32_Process.Create`, Task Scheduler, `wsl.exe`, `docker run`, ShellExecute to an already-running
  application — survives it. Release is a human act for this reason.
- **L5 (W3):** a cell's background processes do not outlive its entry on Windows. Consequences: a harness timeout on the entry ends the cell (the Claude
  Code shell tools stop a foreground command at 2 minutes by default and 10 at most), so long cells are launched as background tasks; a cell child that
  asks for `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` fails; a cell ended mid-write can leave `.git/index.lock`, which the witness tree does not show.
- **L6 (W2):** an entry that dies in the instant between `Popen(CREATE_SUSPENDED)` and the assignment leaves a suspended `cmd.exe` outside the job; it
  runs nothing, inherits no handle, and nothing ends it. The run has no `start` record, so nothing reads it as open.
- **L7 (W4):** if the entry is in a job whose limits forbid nested assignment of its child, launching fails closed; the probes ran nested and passed.
- **L8 (X1, W5):** locks or jobs on a git dir shared across hosts or sessions are outside the design. Entries that take different lock mechanisms on one
  clone do not exclude each other (a WSL Python with `flock` on drvfs, or a Cygwin/MSYS Python, against a native Windows Python); run bomdd-run on one
  clone from one kind of Python.
- **L9 (S1, S3):** if the entry dies after the cell exits but before `end`, the run reads `ABNORMAL_END` and its exit and report binding are lost on release;
  a `--report` path that then exists makes the next launch `ARG_ERROR` (R10), and the operator moves it as evidence.
- **L10 (J2, X3):** a sequential relaunch after a completed or released run is not refused; a dry run's classification can make a concurrent launch read
  `ENTRY_ALIVE`.
- **L11 (X1, J1, R4):** deleting the lock file or the journal by hand is outside the trust boundary; the journal is clone-local; `--by` is self-reported.
- **L12 (T1):** the bomdd-run and bomdd-job selftests are not run in CI; they are run locally and recorded (V5).

### Not changed

- `bomdd-witness.py`, `self-conformance.py`, hooks, `.github`, the playbook, skills, `.claude/skills`, the templates other than operator-layer.md.
- Machine distribution to product repositories (EXP-20260914-01 stays suspended).
- No scheduler, workflow engine, LLM wiki or context access control (user condition).

"""ECO-113 loop 5: mechanical check of S4 (refusals before decide()) against the rest of the order.

Usage: python -B refusal_matrix.py <order.md> <out.md>
Exit 0 = every check passes, 1 = a check fails, 2 = the order cannot be parsed.

Checks:
 C1 the set of refusal reasons that the order DEFINES before decide() == the set of rows in S4's table.
    Defined = every `cause \`X\`` in X2's bullet + every class bullet (`  - \`X\` —`) in J2's bullet + REPORT_EXISTS for S1's
    "re-check `--report`" step (the one pre-decide step of S1 that is neither X2 nor J2; the mapping is fixed here and printed).
 C2 every row has all five columns non-empty.
 C3 every row's "arises in" names a rule whose text contains the reason (REPORT_EXISTS: S1's text contains "re-check `--report`").
 C4 every rule or limit ID cited in a row's "way out" exists as a heading in the order (`- **ID —` or `- **ID (`).
 C5 O1 names every reason (its verdict and exit).
 C6 every reason is named in at least one acceptance item (§3) besides the coverage line.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

src = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
out_path = Path(sys.argv[2])


def bullet(rule_id):
    m = re.search(r"^- \*\*" + re.escape(rule_id) + r" —.*?(?=^- \*\*|^### |^## )", src, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(0) if m else None


fails, notes = [], []
x2, j2, s1, o1 = bullet("X2"), bullet("J2"), bullet("S1"), bullet("O1")
s4 = re.search(r"^- \*\*S4 —.*?(?=^### )", src, re.S | re.M)
acc = re.search(r"^## 3\. Acceptance.*?(?=^## )", src, re.S | re.M)
if not all([x2, j2, s1, o1, s4, acc]):
    print("UNMEASURABLE: a required section was not found", [n for n, v in (("X2", x2), ("J2", j2), ("S1", s1), ("O1", o1),
                                                                          ("S4", s4), ("§3", acc)) if not v])
    sys.exit(2)
s4, acc = s4.group(0), acc.group(0)

defined = {}
for r in re.findall(r"cause `([A-Z_]+)`", x2):
    defined[r] = "X2"
for r in re.findall(r"^\s+- `([A-Z_]+)` —", j2, re.M):
    defined[r] = "J2"
if "re-check `--report`" in s1:
    defined["REPORT_EXISTS"] = "S1"
    notes.append("S1's pre-decide step 're-check `--report`' is mapped to REPORT_EXISTS (fixed in this script)")

rows = {}
for line in s4.splitlines():
    cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")] if line.strip().startswith("| `") else None
    if cells and len(cells) == 5:
        reason = re.match(r"`([A-Z_]+)`", cells[0])
        if reason:
            rows[reason.group(1)] = cells

matrix = []
c1 = set(defined) == set(rows)
if not c1:
    fails.append(f"C1 defined - table: {sorted(set(defined) - set(rows))}; table - defined: {sorted(set(rows) - set(defined))}")
coverage_line = re.search(r"\*\*Coverage \(T1\).*?(?=\n\n)", acc, re.S)
acc_items = acc.replace(coverage_line.group(0), "") if coverage_line else acc
headings = set(re.findall(r"^- \*\*([A-Z][A-Z0-9]*\d+)[ (—]", src, re.M))
for reason in sorted(set(defined) | set(rows)):
    cells = rows.get(reason)
    r = {"reason": reason, "defined_in": defined.get(reason, "-"), "row": bool(cells)}
    if cells:
        r["c2"] = all(cells)
        arises = cells[1]
        rule = re.match(r"([A-Z]\d)", arises)
        body = bullet(rule.group(1)) if rule else None
        r["c3"] = bool(body) and ((reason in body) or (reason == "REPORT_EXISTS" and "re-check `--report`" in body))
        cited = set(re.findall(r"\b([A-Z]\d+)\b", cells[4])) - {"R10", "R7", "R4", "R5", "R8", "R3"} | (
            {"R2"} if "(R2)" in cells[4] else set()) | ({"R3"} if "(R3)" in cells[4] else set())
        cited = set(re.findall(r"\(([A-Z]\d+)\)", cells[4])) | set(re.findall(r"quarantine \(([A-Z]\d+)\)", cells[4]))
        missing = sorted(c for c in cited if c not in headings)
        r["c4"] = not missing
        r["way_out_cites"] = sorted(cited)
        if missing:
            fails.append(f"C4 {reason}: way out cites {missing}, not a heading")
        if not r["c2"]:
            fails.append(f"C2 {reason}: an empty column")
        if not r["c3"]:
            fails.append(f"C3 {reason}: 'arises in' {arises!r} does not name a rule that contains it")
    r["c5"] = reason in o1
    r["c6"] = reason in acc_items
    if not r["c5"]:
        fails.append(f"C5 {reason}: not named in O1")
    if not r["c6"]:
        fails.append(f"C6 {reason}: no acceptance item names it")
    matrix.append(r)

lines = ["| reason | defined in | S4 row | C2 columns | C3 arises-in | C4 way out (cites) | C5 in O1 | C6 in §3 items |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
for r in matrix:
    lines.append(f"| `{r['reason']}` | {r['defined_in']} | {r['row']} | {r.get('c2')} | {r.get('c3')} | {r.get('c4')} {r.get('way_out_cites', '')} "
                 f"| {r['c5']} | {r['c6']} |")
verdict = "PASS" if not fails else "FAIL"
report = [f"# S4 refusal matrix — {verdict}", "", f"C1 (defined == table): {c1}", ""] + lines + ["", "Notes:"] + [f"- {n}" for n in notes] + \
         ["", "Failures:"] + ([f"- {f}" for f in fails] or ["- none"])
out_path.write_text("\n".join(report) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("\n".join(report))
sys.exit(0 if not fails else 1)

r"""ECO-113 loop 5: mechanical check of S4 (refusals before decide()) against the rest of the order.

Usage: python -B refusal_matrix.py <order.md> <out.md>
The verdict is the report's first line (`# S4 refusal matrix — PASS|FAIL|UNMEASURABLE`); the exit code mirrors it (0/1/2).

What it checks (and what it does not):
 C1 the reasons the order DEFINES == the rows of S4's table. "Defined" follows S4's own convention: every phrase  cause `X`  anywhere in §1,
    plus every class bullet of J2. It does NOT prove that no other refusal exists in the code; it proves the order's text and its table agree.
 C2 every row has all five columns non-empty.
 C3 every row's "arises in" names a rule whose text contains the reason.
 C4 every rule or limit cited in a row's "way out" exists as a heading; and if the way out cites R2, R2 does not refuse that reason.
 C5 O1 gives each reason exactly one verdict group (`A`, `B`: `VERDICT`, ... exit N), with STOP → exit 1 and UNMEASURABLE → exit 2.
 C6 every reason is named in at least one acceptance item (§3) besides the coverage line.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
except (AttributeError, ValueError):
    pass

src = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
out_path = Path(sys.argv[2])


def bullet(rule_id):
    m = re.search(r"^- \*\*" + re.escape(rule_id) + r" —.*?(?=^- \*\*|^### |^## )", src, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(0) if m else None


def finish(verdict, body):
    text = "\n".join([f"# S4 refusal matrix — {verdict}", ""] + body) + "\n"
    out_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(text, end="")
    sys.exit({"PASS": 0, "FAIL": 1}.get(verdict, 2))


sec1 = re.search(r"^## 1\. .*?(?=^## 2\.)", src, re.S | re.M)
j2, o1, r2 = bullet("J2"), bullet("O1"), bullet("R2")
s4 = re.search(r"^- \*\*S4 —.*?(?=^### )", src, re.S | re.M)
acc = re.search(r"^## 3\. Acceptance.*?(?=^## )", src, re.S | re.M)
missing = [n for n, v in (("§1", sec1), ("J2", j2), ("O1", o1), ("R2", r2), ("S4", s4), ("§3", acc)) if not v]
if missing:
    finish("UNMEASURABLE", [f"a required section was not found: {missing}"])
sec1, s4, acc = sec1.group(0), s4.group(0), acc.group(0)

defined = {}
for m in re.finditer(r"cause `([A-Z_]+)`", sec1):
    rule = None
    for rm in re.finditer(r"^- \*\*([A-Z]\d+) —", sec1[: m.start()], re.M):
        rule = rm.group(1)
    defined.setdefault(m.group(1), rule or "?")
for r in re.findall(r"^\s+- `([A-Z_]+)` —", j2, re.M):
    defined.setdefault(r, "J2")

rows = {}
for line in s4.splitlines():
    if line.strip().startswith("| `"):
        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        m = re.match(r"`([A-Z_]+)`", cells[0])
        if m and len(cells) == 5:
            rows[m.group(1)] = cells

# O1 verdict groups: "`A`, `B`: `VERDICT`, ... exit N"
groups = []
for m in re.finditer(r"((?:`[A-Z_]+`(?:, )?)+): `(STOP|UNMEASURABLE)[^`]*`[^.]*?exit (\d)", o1):
    groups.append((re.findall(r"`([A-Z_]+)`", m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3)))
r2_refused = set(re.findall(r"`([A-Z_]+)` refused", r2))
headings = set(re.findall(r"^- \*\*([A-Z][A-Z0-9]*\d+)[ (—]", src, re.M))
cov = re.search(r"\*\*Coverage \(T1\).*?(?=\n\n)", acc, re.S)
acc_items = acc.replace(cov.group(0), "") if cov else acc

fails, matrix = [], []
c1 = set(defined) == set(rows)
if not c1:
    fails.append(f"C1 defined - table: {sorted(set(defined) - set(rows))}; table - defined: {sorted(set(rows) - set(defined))}")
for reason in sorted(set(defined) | set(rows)):
    cells = rows.get(reason)
    r = {"reason": reason, "defined_in": defined.get(reason, "-"), "row": bool(cells)}
    if cells:
        r["c2"] = all(cells)
        rule = re.match(r"([A-Z]\d)", cells[1])
        body = bullet(rule.group(1)) if rule else None
        r["c3"] = bool(body) and reason in body
        cited = set(re.findall(r"\(([A-Z]\d+)\)", cells[4]))
        bad_cite = sorted(c for c in cited if c not in headings)
        refused = "R2" in cited and reason in r2_refused
        r["c4"] = not bad_cite and not refused
        r["cites"] = sorted(cited)
        if not r["c2"]:
            fails.append(f"C2 {reason}: an empty column")
        if not r["c3"]:
            fails.append(f"C3 {reason}: 'arises in' {cells[1]!r} does not name a rule that contains it")
        if bad_cite:
            fails.append(f"C4 {reason}: way out cites {bad_cite}, not a heading")
        if refused:
            fails.append(f"C4 {reason}: way out cites R2, which refuses {reason}")
    hits = [(v, e) for names, v, e in groups if reason in names]
    r["c5"] = len(hits) == 1 and ((hits[0][0] == "STOP") == (hits[0][1] == "1"))
    r["o1"] = hits
    if not r["c5"]:
        fails.append(f"C5 {reason}: O1 verdict groups {hits} (need exactly one; STOP→1, UNMEASURABLE→2)")
    r["c6"] = reason in acc_items
    if not r["c6"]:
        fails.append(f"C6 {reason}: no acceptance item names it")
    matrix.append(r)

lines = [f"C1 (defined == table): {c1}", "",
         "| reason | defined in | S4 row | C2 | C3 | C4 (cites) | C5 (O1) | C6 |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
for r in matrix:
    lines.append(f"| `{r['reason']}` | {r['defined_in']} | {r['row']} | {r.get('c2')} | {r.get('c3')} | {r.get('c4')} {r.get('cites', '')} "
                 f"| {r['c5']} {r['o1']} | {r['c6']} |")
lines += ["", "Failures:"] + ([f"- {f}" for f in fails] or ["- none"])
finish("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL", lines)

import shutil
import subprocess

from pathlib import Path

repo_tools = Path(sys.argv[1])
work = Path(sys.argv[2])
cases = {
    "G3-off": ('    if rec["job_state"] == "verified":   # ECO-112 G3', '    if False:   # ECO-112 G3', "g3-"),
    "B4-off": ('        res, bcode, bmsg = committed_copies(root, common, eco, rec["tree"])',

                 '    rec, job = decide(root, eco, jobmod, witmod, executor)\n', "--report はリポ相対パ"),
}
bad = 0
for name, (old, new, expect) in cases.items():
    d = work / name
    if d.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    shutil.copytree(repo_tools, d, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))
    p = d / "bomdd-run.py"
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert s.count(old) == 1, (name, old[:60])
    p.write_text(s.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(p), "--selftest"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
                       env={**__import__("os").environ, "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8"})
    red = r.returncode != 0 and r.stdout.startswith("STOP SELFTEST_FAIL")
    named = expect in r.stdout
    bad += not (red and named)
    print(f"{name}: exit {r.returncode}, red {red}, names {expect!r} {named} :: {r.stdout.splitlines()[0][:70] if r.stdout else ''}")
print("rule mutations", "PASS" if not bad else f"FAIL ({bad})")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

r"""ECO-113: mechanical check that the receipt's evidence records match the evidence files, and that a record fix leaves the design unchanged.

Usage:
  python -B record_check.py design-hash <order.md>            print sha256 of everything before "## 収束 receipt" (the design: header..§3)
  python -B record_check.py evidence <order.md> <dir>         every sha256 prefix the order states for an evidence file must be that file's sha256,
                                                              and every evidence file must be named with its current sha256 at least once
Exit 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL. The verdict is also the output's first line.
"""
import hashlib
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
except (AttributeError, ValueError):
    pass

mode, order = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2])
text = order.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
cut = text.find("\n## 収束 receipt")
if cut < 0:
    print("UNMEASURABLE: no receipt heading")
    sys.exit(2)
if mode == "design-hash":
    print(hashlib.sha256(text[:cut].encode("utf-8")).hexdigest())
    sys.exit(0)

evdir = Path(sys.argv[3])
names = ("refusal_matrix.py", "calibrate_matrix.py", "refusal-matrix.md")
actual = {n: hashlib.sha256((evdir / n).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for n in names}
receipt = text[cut:]
fails, lines = [], []
# every "<name>` ... sha256 `<hex>…`" and "<name>` (sha256 `<hex>…`)" mention, and the parenthesised "(`<name>`, sha256 `<hex>…`)" form
for m in re.finditer(r"`(refusal_matrix\.py|calibrate_matrix\.py|refusal-matrix\.md)`[^`\n]{0,40}?sha256 `([0-9a-f]{8,64})…?`", receipt):
    name, pref = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    ok = actual[name].startswith(pref)
    lines.append(f"{name}: stated {pref} actual {actual[name][:16]} -> {'OK' if ok else 'MISMATCH'}")
    if not ok:
        fails.append(f"{name}: stated {pref} != actual {actual[name][:16]}")
# bare prefixes stated next to a name in a "Script sha256 `x`; report `y`" sentence
for m in re.finditer(r"Script sha256 `([0-9a-f]{8,64})…?`; report `([0-9a-f]{8,64})…?`", receipt):
    for name, pref in (("refusal_matrix.py", m.group(1)), ("refusal-matrix.md", m.group(2))):
        ok = actual[name].startswith(pref)
        lines.append(f"{name}: stated {pref} actual {actual[name][:16]} -> {'OK' if ok else 'MISMATCH'}")
        if not ok:
            fails.append(f"{name}: stated {pref} != actual {actual[name][:16]}")
for n in names:
    if not any(n in ln and "OK" in ln for ln in lines):
        fails.append(f"{n}: its current sha256 is not stated in the receipt")
print("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL")
print("\n".join(lines))
for f in fails:
    print("FAIL:", f)
sys.exit(0 if not fails else 1)

from pathlib import Path
import sys

p = Path(sys.argv[1])
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def rep(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:80]
    s = s.replace(old, new)


rep("""  compare. Any failure → the decision becomes `UNMEASURABLE` before the decision record is written (code `BRIEF_UNREADABLE`, `BRIEF_NOT_LF` or
  `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`, stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, delivery operator), and nothing launches.""",
    """  compare. Any failure → the decision becomes `UNMEASURABLE` before the decision record is written (code `BRIEF_UNREADABLE`, `BRIEF_NOT_LF` or
  `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`, stop type `MISSING_INPUT`, delivery operator), and nothing launches.
  **Rollback (amendment, IA-01):** the invocation notes whether **it created** the stored file (the final name did not exist when it looked, and its own
  `os.replace` put it there). If anything after storing fails before the cell starts — the execution copy (B3) or the decision record (the existing
  ledger-failure path) — nothing launches and the invocation removes the stored file **only if it created it**; a file that already existed is left as
  it was. If that removal fails, the invocation prints, after its existing first line, the line `brief left in store: <sha256 prefix> (<OS error>)`, and
  the exit stays 2. The left file then makes B4 demand a committed copy at promotion; the recorded way out is to remove it by hand after checking that no
  decision record of the ECO names its sha256.""")
rep("""- **B3 — the record.** The decision record carries `brief: {path, sha256, size, store_ref}`; `store_ref` is the stored file's path, the reference from
  which the original bytes are re-fetched on this clone. The cell receives `BOMDD_BRIEF` = that path. The store directory's 64-hex files are the set of
  briefs launched for the ECO on this clone (no index file).""",
    """- **B3 — the record, and two copies (amendment, IA-02).** The decision record carries `brief: {path, sha256, size, store_ref}`; `store_ref` is the
  stored file's path — the **archival copy**, the reference from which the original bytes are re-fetched on this clone. The cell is **never** given
  `store_ref`: after storing and before the decision record, the invocation writes an **execution copy** — the same bytes in a new file inside a fresh
  temporary directory outside the worktree and outside the store — re-hashes it, and passes that file as `BOMDD_BRIEF`. After the cell exits, the
  execution copy and its directory are removed (a removal failure is ignored; the OS temporary area holds it). A failure to write or re-hash the execution
  copy → `UNMEASURABLE`, `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED`, recorded in the decision record, no launch, and B2's rollback applies. Whatever the cell does to the file
  it was given, the archival copy is untouched. The store directory's 64-hex files are the set of briefs launched for the ECO on this clone (no index file).""")
rep("""- **L4 (B2, B4):** the store is clone-local; on another clone B4 sees an empty store and checks nothing. A brief deleted from the store by hand is outside
  the trust boundary (like deleting the witness, ECO-046).""",
    """- **L4 (B2, B3, B4):** the store is clone-local; on another clone B4 sees an empty store and checks nothing. The cell is handed an execution copy, so a
  cell that deletes or changes what it was given loses nothing (V2(i)). A brief deleted from the store by hand — or by a cell that seeks out
  `<git-common-dir>/bomdd-run/briefs/` on purpose — is outside the trust boundary (like deleting the witness, ECO-046); B4 then sees fewer stored
  briefs and checks only those.
- **L10 (B2's rollback):** until ECO-113's exclusion exists, two concurrent launches of one ECO with the same brief can race on the stored file: if the one
  that created it then fails before its cell starts, its rollback removes a file the other launch's cell was recorded with. The other cell still has its
  own execution copy; the archival copy of that brief is then missing from the store, and B4 does not check it (L4).""")
rep("""  (f) **real cells, before promotion:** the independent-inspection cells for this ECO run with `--brief`, and each brief re-fetched from its `store_ref`
      has the sha256 the ledger records.""",
    """  (f) **real cells, before promotion:** the independent-inspection cells for this ECO run with `--brief`, and each brief re-fetched from its `store_ref`
      has the sha256 the ledger records;
  (g) **rollback (IA-01):** a real brief with an unwritable ledger → no launch, exit 2, and no stored file for that brief afterwards; the same with the
      brief already in the store before that invocation → the stored file is still there with its bytes; the execution copy failing (patched) → no launch,
      `BRIEF_STORE_FAILED` in the decision record, and no stored file created by that invocation is left;
  (h) **rollback failure:** the removal failing (patched) → the line `brief left in store: <sha256 prefix> (…)` after the first line, exit 2, and the file
      still in the store;
  (i) **two copies (IA-02):** the cell's `BOMDD_BRIEF` is not `store_ref` and lies outside the worktree and the store, with the brief's bytes; a cell that
      deletes `BOMDD_BRIEF` → the archival copy is still in the store with its bytes, and the next promotion still demands its committed copy
      (`BRIEF_NOT_COMMITTED` until it is committed);
  (j) the execution copy and its directory are gone after the cell exits.""")
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("ok")

  `os.replace` put it there). If one of two steps fails after storing — the execution copy (B3) or the decision record (the existing ledger-failure
  path) — nothing launches and the invocation removes the stored file **only if it created it**; a file that already existed is left as it was. If the
  rollback's removal fails, the invocation prints, after its existing first line, the line `brief left in store: <sha256 prefix> (<OS error>)`, and the
  exit stays 2. A cell that fails to start after the decision record is written (`cell_exit: "OSError: …"` in its cell record) is not rolled back; it
  was launched (bomdd-run R8) and its brief stays in the store. **In both cases the brief left in the store is resolved the same way:** B4 demands its
  committed copy at promotion, and committing the brief under `bomdd/reports/` satisfies it (it adds evidence and removes nothing). No removal by hand is
  part of the procedure.
"""
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("ok")

"""ECO-112 V6 under the user's exception ruling (2026-10-18, "A"): the change set is the commits attributed to ECO-112 only.

Usage: python -B diff_window.py <repo> <baseline> <head>   (prints the evidence as Markdown; exit 0 = every check holds)

Attribution is by the commit subject's tag, "(eco-112)" or another "(eco-NNN)"; a commit with no tag is reported and fails the run.
Checks:
  C1 every commit in baseline..head is attributed; the excluded set is exactly the commits of other ECOs (listed with their reason).
  C2 an excluded commit touches no ECO-112 allowed path except the shared register, and there only adds lines inside its own ECO's entry;
     the ECO-112 register entry is byte-identical before and after it.
  C3 no ECO-112 commit touches a path an excluded commit introduced, and those paths are unchanged from the excluded commit to head.
  C4 every path changed by an ECO-112 commit is inside the register's ECO-112 diff_audit.allowed_paths (V6).
  C5 the net diff baseline..head, with the excluded commits' own entry removed from the register, changes only ECO-112's paths and,
     in the register, only the ECO-112 entry.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys

REPO, BASE, HEAD = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
ECO = "ECO-112"
REG = "bomdd/60-change-register.yaml"
TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\((eco-\d{3})\)")


def git(*a, binary=False):
    r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"git {' '.join(a)} failed: {r.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}")
    return r.stdout if binary else r.stdout.decode("utf-8")


def entry(text, eco):
    """The register entry block of eco: from its '  - id: ECO-NNN' line to the next entry line (exclusive)."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    start = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l == f"  - id: {eco}"), None)
    if start is None:
        return None, lines
    end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith("  - id: ")), len(lines))
    return (start, end), lines


def allowed_paths(rev):
    reg = git("show", f"{rev}:{REG}")
    span, lines = entry(reg, ECO)
    blk = "\n".join(lines[span[0]:span[1]])
    m = re.search(r"allowed_paths: \[([^\]]*)\]", blk)
    return [p.strip() for p in m.group(1).split(",")]


def inside(path, allowed):
    return any(path == a or (a.endswith("/") and path.startswith(a)) for a in allowed)


out, bad = [], []
commits = [ln.split(" ", 1) for ln in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H %s", f"{BASE}..{HEAD}").splitlines()]
allowed = allowed_paths(HEAD)
own, excluded = [], []
out.append(f"# ECO-112 diff window under the exception ruling — `{BASE}..{HEAD[:12]}`\n")
out.append(f"ECO-112 `diff_audit.allowed_paths` (register at `{HEAD[:12]}`): " + ", ".join(f"`{a}`" for a in allowed) + "\n")
out.append("| commit | attributed to | paths changed |\n|---|---|---|")
for sha, subj in commits:
    tags = TAG_RE.findall(subj)
    files = [ln.split("\t", 1)[1] for ln in git("diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "-r", "--name-status", sha).splitlines()]
    who = tags[0].upper() if len(set(tags)) == 1 else None
    if who is None:
        bad.append(f"C1: {sha[:7]} has no single ECO tag: {subj[:60]}")
    (own if who == ECO else excluded).append((sha, subj, files, who))
    out.append(f"| `{sha[:7]}` | {who or '?'} | {len(files)} |")

out.append("\n## Excluded commits (C1) and why\n")
for sha, subj, files, who in excluded:
    out.append(f"- `{sha[:7]}` — {who}: {subj[:100]}… — another ECO's filing, outside ECO-112's manufacture (user ruling 2026-10-18 \"A\").")

out.append("\n## C2 — the excluded commits against ECO-112's paths and register entry\n")
for sha, subj, files, who in excluded:
    shared = [f for f in files if inside(f, allowed)]
    out.append(f"- `{sha[:7]}`: paths inside ECO-112's allowed paths: {shared or 'none'}")
    if any(f != REG for f in shared):
        bad.append(f"C2: {sha[:7]} touches ECO-112 paths {shared}")
    if REG in files:
        before, after = git("show", f"{sha}^:{REG}"), git("show", f"{sha}:{REG}")
        sb, lb = entry(before, ECO)
        sa, la = entry(after, ECO)
        same = lb[sb[0]:sb[1]] == la[sa[0]:sa[1]]
        diff = git("diff", "-U0", f"{sha}^", sha, "--", REG)
        removed = [l for l in diff.splitlines() if l.startswith("-") and not l.startswith("---")]
        hunks = [tuple(int(x or 1) for x in m.groups()) for m in re.finditer(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@", diff, re.M)]
        own_span, _ = entry(after, who)
        within = all(own_span and own_span[0] + 1 <= s and s + n - 1 <= own_span[1] for s, n in hunks)
        out.append(f"  - register: removed lines {len(removed)}; added hunks {hunks} inside {who}'s entry (lines {own_span[0] + 1}-{own_span[1]}): "
                   f"{within}; ECO-112 entry byte-identical before/after: {same}")
        if removed or not within or not same:
            bad.append(f"C2: {sha[:7]} register change is not confined to its own entry")

out.append("\n## C3 — paths the excluded commits introduced, after them\n")
for sha, subj, files, who in excluded:
    theirs = [f for f in files if f != REG]
    touched_by_own = sorted({f for _, _, fs, _ in own for f in fs} & set(theirs))
    later = git("diff", "--name-only", sha, HEAD, "--", *theirs).split() if theirs else []
    out.append(f"- `{sha[:7]}`: {len(theirs)} paths; touched by an ECO-112 commit: {touched_by_own or 'none'}; changed between `{sha[:7]}` and head: {later or 'none'}")
    if touched_by_own or later:
        bad.append(f"C3: {sha[:7]} paths touched later: {touched_by_own or later}")

out.append("\n## C4 — the ECO-112 change set, enumerated (V6)\n")
changed = {}
for sha, subj, files, who in own:
    for f in files:
        changed.setdefault(f, []).append(sha[:7])
for f in sorted(changed):
    ok = inside(f, allowed)
    out.append(f"- `{f}` — {', '.join(changed[f])}" + ("" if ok else " **OUTSIDE**"))
    if not ok:
        bad.append(f"C4: {f} outside allowed_paths")
out.append(f"\nECO-112 commits: {len(own)} ({', '.join(f'`{s[:7]}`' for s, _, _, _ in own)}); paths: {len(changed)}.")

out.append("\n## C5 — the net diff without the excluded commits' own entries\n")
net = [ln.split("\t", 1) for ln in git("diff", "--name-status", BASE, HEAD).splitlines()]
excl_paths = {f for _, _, fs, _ in excluded for f in fs if f != REG}
net_paths = sorted(p for _, p in net if p not in excl_paths)
outside = [p for p in net_paths if not inside(p, allowed)]
reg_b, reg_h = git("show", f"{BASE}:{REG}"), git("show", f"{HEAD}:{REG}")
lines_h = reg_h.split("\n")
for _, _, _, who in excluded:
    sp, lines_h = entry("\n".join(lines_h), who)
    if sp:
        lines_h = lines_h[:sp[0]] + lines_h[sp[1]:]
sb, lb = entry(reg_b, ECO)
sh, lh = entry("\n".join(lines_h), ECO)
rest_same = lb[:sb[0]] + lb[sb[1]:] == lh[:sh[0]] + lh[sh[1]:]
out.append(f"- net paths (excluded commits' own paths removed): {len(net_paths)}; outside ECO-112's allowed paths: {outside or 'none'}")
out.append(f"- register with the excluded ECOs' entries removed: everything outside the ECO-112 entry equals the baseline: {rest_same}")
if outside or not rest_same:
    bad.append(f"C5: net diff outside ECO-112: {outside} / register rest same {rest_same}")

out.append("\n## Result\n")
out.append("**PASS** — every check holds." if not bad else "**FAIL**\n" + "\n".join(f"- {b}" for b in bad))
sys.stdout.buffer.write(("\n".join(out) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

"""Effort measurement of one Claude Code session transcript (observed values only).

Usage: python -B session_effort.py <session.jsonl> <subagents dir> > out.md

Partition of the session's wall clock into three states, by what ends each idle gap:
  AI_ACTIVE   from a turn's start (a human message, a task notification or a peer report) to the last assistant/tool record of that turn
  BG_WAIT     idle gap ended by a task notification or a peer (subagent) report: the AI had ended its turn to wait for background work
  HUMAN_WAIT  idle gap ended by a human message
Inside AI_ACTIVE: tool execution (tool_use -> its tool_result) by tool and by Bash description class; the rest is model time
(generation, thinking, harness overhead). Background Bash tasks: start (the tool_use with run_in_background) -> its notification.
Tokens: assistant records deduplicated by requestId (one API call is split into several records).
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

JST = timedelta(hours=9)
SRC, SUBDIR = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])


def ts(s):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))


def fmt(td):
    s = int(td.total_seconds()) if isinstance(td, timedelta) else int(td)
    return f"{s // 3600}:{s % 3600 // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}"


recs = [json.loads(ln) for ln in SRC.open(encoding="utf-8")]
ev = [r for r in recs if r.get("timestamp") and r.get("type") in ("user", "assistant", "system", "attachment")]
ev.sort(key=lambda r: r["timestamp"])


def kind(r):
    if r["type"] == "user":
        m = r["message"].get("content")
        if isinstance(m, list) and any(x.get("type") == "tool_result" for x in m):
            return "tool_result"
        return (r.get("origin") or {}).get("kind") or "user-other"
    return r["type"]


STARTERS = {"human", "task-notification", "peer"}
t0, t1 = ts(ev[0]["timestamp"]), ts(ev[-1]["timestamp"])
state = Counter()
gaps = []           # (start, end, ender)
turns = []          # (start, end, starter, text)
last_active = ts(ev[0]["timestamp"])
cur = None
for r in ev:
    k, t = kind(r), ts(r["timestamp"])
    if k in STARTERS:
        if cur:
            turns.append(cur)
        gap = t - last_active
        state["HUMAN_WAIT" if k == "human" else "BG_WAIT"] += gap.total_seconds()
        gaps.append((last_active, t, k))
        m = r["message"].get("content")
        cur = [t, t, k, (m if isinstance(m, str) else "")[:70].replace("\n", " ")]
        last_active = t
    else:
        if cur is None:
            cur = [t, t, "start", ""]
        if r["type"] in ("assistant", "user", "system"):
            state["AI_ACTIVE"] += (t - last_active).total_seconds()
            last_active = t
            cur[1] = t
if cur:
    turns.append(cur)

# tool execution inside turns
uses = {}
tool_time = defaultdict(float)
tool_n = Counter()
bash_class_time = defaultdict(float)
bash_class_n = Counter()
bg_start = {}
bg_tasks = []
CLASSES = [
    ("self-conformance", re.compile(r"self-conformance", re.I)),
    ("CI wait", re.compile(r"gh run list|Wait for CI", re.I)),
    ("V3 instrument", re.compile(r"arm_inventory|V3 instrument|pinned V3", re.I)),
    ("inspection cell (codex)", re.compile(r"codex exec|independent inspection", re.I)),
    ("rule mutations", re.compile(r"rule.?mutation|Break each new rule", re.I)),
    ("selftests", re.compile(r"--selftest|selftests?", re.I)),
    ("git commit/push", re.compile(r"git (commit|push)|Commit and push", re.I)),
    ("witness/decision", re.compile(r"bomdd-witness|bomdd-run.py ECO-1", re.I)),

payload:
"""When did the text each design-review finding points at first appear? (ECO-112 / ECO-113 design reviews, 2026-10-18)

Usage: python -B measure_origin.py <dir>     (<dir> holds primary/, round_map.json and baseline/; writes findings.jsonl and summary.md there)

Two axes, kept apart (user ruling 2026-10-18 "A"):
  origin time   INITIAL  every traced quote existed before the ECO's first review request (the first reviewed version)
                LATER    every traced quote first appeared after that request (in a version produced by a repair); the version is named
                UNKNOWN  no quote, no quote traceable to a write before this round's request, quotes that disagree, or counts that do not match
  cause         copied from the record only (the reviewer's tag in the finding, or the order's "Classes in this loop" line):
                FIX_CHANGE  "new defect from the consolidation", "new defect from the amendment", or a note "introduced by ... repair"
                EXISTING    "existing design defect" with no such note
                UNKNOWN     nothing recorded ("inconsistency from duplicated text" is kept as the type DUPLICATION, its cause UNKNOWN)
How a quote is traced: the finding's quoted strings ("…" or “…”, split at ellipses, at least MIN chars after normalising whitespace, backticks
and asterisks) are searched in the payloads of every file-writing call of the main session (primary/edits.jsonl: Write content, Edit new_string,
Bash/PowerShell command) up to this round's review request; the earliest payload containing it is the quote's first appearance. A quote found
only in the repository's baseline files (baseline/) is repository text, not design text, and is not used; a quote first found after the round's
request (a proposed wording, or a paraphrase that matches later text) is not used; a quote found nowhere is not used. Nothing is guessed.
Limit (stated in summary.md): the time measured is the quoted text's, not the defect's; a defect in old text caused by a later change elsewhere
reads INITIAL here unless the finding also quotes the new text (then the quotes disagree and it reads UNKNOWN).
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(sys.argv[1])
MIN = 15
ID_RE = re.compile(r"^\W{0,4}(F\d+|R\d+-\d+|L\dR\d+-\d+|AR\d+-\d+|A1R\d+-\d+)\b")
QUOTE_RE = re.compile(r"\"([^\"\n]{%d,600})\"|“([^”]{%d,600})”" % (MIN, MIN))
HEAD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*findings:\s*(\d+)", re.I | re.M)
SEV_RE = re.compile(r"\[(material|minor)\]|—\s*(material|minor)\s*—", re.I)
TAGS = [("new defect from the consolidation", "FIX_CHANGE"), ("new defect from the amendment", "FIX_CHANGE"),
        ("existing design defect", "EXISTING"), ("inconsistency from duplicated text", "DUPLICATION")]


def norm(s):
    s = s.replace("`", "").replace("**", "").replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'")
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip(" .,;:")


def frags(q):
    return [f for f in (norm(p) for p in re.split(r"…|\.\.\.", q)) if len(f) >= MIN]


rmap = json.loads((D / "round_map.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
reviews = [json.loads(ln) for ln in (D / "primary" / "reviews.jsonl").open(encoding="utf-8")]
edits = [json.loads(ln) for ln in (D / "primary" / "edits.jsonl").open(encoding="utf-8")]
for e in edits:
    e["_n"] = norm(e["payload"])
baseline = {p.name: norm(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in sorted((D / "baseline").glob("*")) if p.is_file()}

by_agent = defaultdict(lambda: {"request": [], "report": []})
for x in reviews:
    by_agent[x["agent"]][x["kind"]].append(x)
eco_first = {}
rounds = []   # (eco, label, request_ts, report)
for agent, kinds in by_agent.items():
    cfg = rmap[agent]
    reqs = sorted(kinds["request"], key=lambda x: x["ts"])
    reps = sorted(kinds["report"], key=lambda x: x["ts"])
    assert len(reps) == len(cfg["rounds"]), (agent, len(reps), len(cfg["rounds"]))
    for label, rep in zip(cfg["rounds"], reps):
        req = max((q for q in reqs if q["ts"] <= rep["ts"]), key=lambda q: q["ts"])
        rounds.append((cfg["eco"], label, req["ts"], rep, agent))
    eco_first[cfg["eco"]] = min(eco_first.get(cfg["eco"], "9"), reqs[0]["ts"])
rounds.sort(key=lambda r: r[2])

# the recorded classes in the orders' receipts: ID -> (class, note)
recorded = {}
for eco, order in (("ECO-112", "order-eco-112.md"), ("ECO-113", "order-eco-113.md")):
    txt = (D / "baseline" / order).read_text(encoding="utf-8") if (D / "baseline" / order).exists() else ""
    for m in re.finditer(r"\*\*Classes in this loop[^:]*:\*\*(.*?)(?=\n- \*\*|\n#|\Z)", txt, re.S):
        body = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", m.group(1))
        for part in re.finditer(r"(new defect from the (?:consolidation|amendment)|existing design defect|inconsistency from duplicated text) \d+ \(([^)]*)\)", body):
            cls = part.group(1)
            for idm in re.finditer(r"(L\dR\d+-\d+|AR\d+-\d+|A1R\d+-\d+)((?:,? [^,;)]*)?)", part.group(2)):
                recorded.setdefault((eco, idm.group(1)), []).append((cls, idm.group(2).strip(", ")))
            rng = re.search(r"(A1R\d)-(\d) to A1R\d-(\d)", part.group(2))
            if rng:
                for k in range(int(rng.group(2)), int(rng.group(3)) + 1):
                    recorded.setdefault((eco, f"{rng.group(1)}-{k}"), []).append((cls, ""))


def trace(fr, cutoff):
    for name, txt in baseline.items():
        if name.startswith("order-"):
            continue
        if fr in txt:
            return {"status": "baseline", "file": name}
    hit = next((e for e in edits if fr in e["_n"]), None)
    if hit is None:
        return {"status": "not_found"}
    ev = {"edit_seq": hit["seq"], "ts": hit["ts"], "tool": hit["tool"], "file_path": hit.get("file_path"), "source": hit["source"]}
    if hit["ts"] > cutoff:
        return dict(ev, status="postdates_request")
    return dict(ev, status="traced")


def version_after(eco, ts):
    """the last review request of this ECO before ts: the text first entered the version reviewed in the next round."""
    prev = [r for r in rounds if r[0] == eco and r[2] < ts]
    return prev[-1][1] if prev else None


findings, mismatches = [], []
for eco, label, req_ts, rep, agent in rounds:
    text = rep["text"]
    head = HEAD_RE.search(text)
    lines = text.split("\n")
    seen = {f["id"] for f in findings if f["agent"] == agent}
    starts = []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = ID_RE.match(l)
        if m:
            starts.append((i, m.group(1)))
    new = [(i, fid) for i, fid in starts if fid not in seen and fid not in {s[1] for s in starts[:starts.index((i, fid))]}]
    want = rmap["receipt_counts"][eco][[r[1] for r in rounds if r[0] == eco].index(label)]
    if len(new) != want or (head and int(head.group(1)) != want):
        mismatches.append(f"{eco} {label}: report header {head.group(1) if head else '?'}, new IDs {len(new)}, receipt {want}")
    for k, (i, fid) in enumerate(new):
        nxt = next((j for j, _ in starts if j > i), len(lines))
        body = "\n".join(lines[i:nxt]).strip()
        sev = SEV_RE.search(body)
        quotes = [q for m in QUOTE_RE.finditer(body) for q in [m.group(1) or m.group(2)]]
        fr_list = [f for q in quotes for f in frags(q)]
        traced = [dict(trace(f, req_ts), fragment=f) for f in dict.fromkeys(fr_list)]
        use = [t for t in traced if t["status"] == "traced"]
        if not quotes:
            origin, reason = "UNKNOWN", "no quoted text in the finding"
        elif not use:
            st = Counter(t["status"] for t in traced)
            origin, reason = "UNKNOWN", "no quote traceable before the round's request (" + ", ".join(f"{k2} {v}" for k2, v in st.items()) + ")"
        else:
            sides = {("INITIAL" if t["ts"] <= eco_first[eco] else "LATER") for t in use}
            if len(sides) > 1:
                origin, reason = "UNKNOWN", "quotes disagree (some before, some after the first review)"
            else:
                origin, reason = sides.pop(), ""
        appeared = None
        if origin == "LATER":
            first = min(use, key=lambda t: t["ts"])
            appeared = {"after_request_of": version_after(eco, first["ts"]), "first_reviewed_in": next(
                (r[1] for r in rounds if r[0] == eco and r[2] >= first["ts"]), None)}
        # cause: the record only
        tag_hits = [(t, c) for t, c in TAGS if t in body.lower()]
        rec = recorded.get((eco, fid), [])
        cause, ftype, cause_src = "UNKNOWN", None, None
        notes = " ".join(n for _, n in rec)
        classes = [c for _, c in tag_hits] + [dict(TAGS)[c] for c, _ in rec]
        if "DUPLICATION" in classes:
            ftype = "DUPLICATION"
        if "introduced by" in notes and "repair" in notes:
            cause, cause_src = "FIX_CHANGE", "receipt note: " + notes
        elif "FIX_CHANGE" in classes and "EXISTING" not in classes:
            cause, cause_src = "FIX_CHANGE", "recorded class"
        elif "EXISTING" in classes and "FIX_CHANGE" not in classes:
            cause, cause_src = "EXISTING", "recorded class"
        findings.append({"eco": eco, "round": label, "id": fid, "agent": agent, "severity": (sev.group(1) or sev.group(2)).lower() if sev else None,
                         "review_request_ts": req_ts, "report_ts": rep["ts"], "report_source": rep["source"],
                         "origin": origin, "origin_reason": reason, "appeared": appeared, "quotes": traced,
                         "cause": cause, "cause_source": cause_src, "type": ftype,
                         "recorded_classes": [c for c, _ in rec] + [t for t, _ in tag_hits], "text": body})

with (D / "findings.jsonl").open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh:
    for f in findings:
        fh.write(json.dumps(f, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

out = []
P = out.append
P("# Review-finding origin — ECO-112 / ECO-113 design reviews (measured 2026-10-19)\n")
P(f"Findings parsed: **{len(findings)}** (ECO-112 {sum(f['eco'] == 'ECO-112' for f in findings)}, ECO-113 {sum(f['eco'] == 'ECO-113' for f in findings)}); "
  f"count checks against the receipts: {'all match' if not mismatches else 'MISMATCH — ' + '; '.join(mismatches)}.")
P(f"First review request: ECO-112 {eco_first['ECO-112']}, ECO-113 {eco_first['ECO-113']} (UTC).\n")
P("## Origin time\n\n| ECO | INITIAL | LATER | UNKNOWN | total |\n|---|---|---|---|---|")
for eco in ("ECO-112", "ECO-113", None):
    fs = [f for f in findings if eco is None or f["eco"] == eco]
    c = Counter(f["origin"] for f in fs)
    P(f"| {eco or 'both'} | {c['INITIAL']} | {c['LATER']} | {c['UNKNOWN']} | {len(fs)} |")
P("\n## By loop\n\n| ECO | loop | rounds | findings | INITIAL | LATER | UNKNOWN |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
loops = defaultdict(list)
for f in findings:
    loops[(f["eco"], re.match(r"(L\d|AR|A2)", f["round"]).group(1))].append(f)
for (eco, lp), fs in sorted(loops.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[0][0], min(f["review_request_ts"] for f in kv[1]))):
    c = Counter(f["origin"] for f in fs)
    nr = len({r[1] for r in rounds if r[0] == eco and r[1].startswith(lp)})
    P(f"| {eco} | {lp} | {nr} | {len(fs)} | {c['INITIAL']} | {c['LATER']} | {c['UNKNOWN']} |")
P("\n## UNKNOWN reasons\n\n| reason | findings |\n|---|---|")
for k, v in Counter(re.sub(r" \(.*", "", f["origin_reason"]) for f in findings if f["origin"] == "UNKNOWN").most_common():
    P(f"| {k} | {v} |")
P("\n## Cause (recorded only) against origin time\n\n| cause | INITIAL | LATER | UNKNOWN | total |\n|---|---|---|---|---|")
for cz in ("FIX_CHANGE", "EXISTING", "UNKNOWN"):
    fs = [f for f in findings if f["cause"] == cz]
    c = Counter(f["origin"] for f in fs)
    P(f"| {cz} | {c['INITIAL']} | {c['LATER']} | {c['UNKNOWN']} | {len(fs)} |")
P(f"\nType DUPLICATION (recorded): {sum(f['type'] == 'DUPLICATION' for f in findings)}.")
P("\n## Severity against origin time\n\n| severity | INITIAL | LATER | UNKNOWN |\n|---|---|---|---|")
for sv in ("material", "minor", None):
    c = Counter(f["origin"] for f in findings if f["severity"] == sv)
    P(f"| {sv or 'not stated'} | {c['INITIAL']} | {c['LATER']} | {c['UNKNOWN']} |")
P("\n## Limits\n")
P("- The time measured is the quoted text's first appearance, not the defect's cause (a defect in old text caused by a later change elsewhere "
  "reads INITIAL unless the new text is also quoted).")
P("- A finding with no quote, or whose quotes are paraphrases, is UNKNOWN; nothing is filled in by reading.")
P("- A quote can match an earlier, unrelated occurrence of the same words; the minimum length is " + str(MIN) + " characters after normalisation.")
P("- The first reviewed version of ECO-113 was written from ECO-112's pre-split draft; text carried over reads INITIAL for ECO-113.")
P("- Severity is the reviewer's tag where one is written; causes are only those recorded, so most causes are UNKNOWN.")
(D / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
